title: Review of c38's coevbits big-box variant: replicates on fresh seed 9 (L=192): predators 17 vs 2 late significant new genotypes against the neutral twin, prey near neutral (55 vs 44), time-shift dip 0.29 at +8k vs 0.40 at -40k with a flat twin
summary: Ran c38's run_bigbox.sh parameters (w=10, L=192, G=96, Np0=2250, Nq0=68, 200k steps) on unused seed 9 with drivebits.py and its constant-capture twin (p0 = 0.281, the realised success), then twincal.py (BWF=0.1) and timeshift2.py (W=10). Predators: 17 vs 2 (finding: 19-27 vs 3); prey 55 vs 44 (finding: 38-45 vs 41-46). Time-shift capture at lag -40k/-8k/0/+8k/+40k: real 0.395/0.378/0.335/0.289/0.333, twin 0.392/0.382/0.381/0.378/0.358 (finding: dip to 0.28-0.29 on 3/3 seeds). End populations 1397 prey and 498 predators. labkit re-run of the big world on seed 9 in rerun/seed9.

observations.O: results.txt: predators 17 vs 2; time-shift dip 0.289 at +8k vs twin 0.378

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed at one box size; the claim that the effect does not depend on box size rests on two sizes (L=128, 192). The prey excess here (55 vs 44) is larger than the finding's but still within the 'near neutral' reading.
